summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR43.8 crore and EBITDA margin hit 47.5%, while the company pursues a debt- and equity-funded acquisition of MicroBiopharm Japan and Sanofi brands.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR43.8 crore (up 22.1% YoY) on higher sales volumes, with EBITDA up 49.4% to INR20.8 crore at a 47.5% margin and PAT of INR11.1 crore (up 22.1%). Management described the business as sold out in capacity for years and said the expanded fermentation capacity (about 540 KL, roughly doubling capacity) starts full operation by end-August 2026. The call focused mostly on the strategic pivot to a fermentation-based CDMO, the MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) acquisition, and the Sanofi brand portfolio, with funding (up to INR1,000 crore equity, debt mix undecided) and deal timing left open.

financial_highlights.change: from about INR62 crore in FY23; about INR370 crore added in 3 years

segments.name: Standalone GTBL - fermentation and API (Rifamycin-S, Rifapentine, Rifaximin)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue has been stuck around the historic INR40 crore run rate; API block bookings are in Rifapentine, Rifaximin and Rifamycin-S. Management said API output began only recently because intermediate capacity was the constraint.

segments.name: MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) - to be acquired
segments.commentary: MBJ is about 100% API CDMO, with roughly 4-5% formulations; 60% of its business is CDMO, and revenue is 60% Japan and 40% outside Japan. Revenue by vertical was not disclosed. ADCs are patented but have no CDMO project yet; other platforms are commercialised.

segments.name: Sanofi brands (13 anti-TB and anti-infective brands)
segments.commentary: Branded generics sold in 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa. Revenue and margin figures were not disclosed. Manufacturing will move to CMOs over a 3-year transition services agreement.

guidance_outlook: Expanded fermentation capacity to be fully operational by end-August 2026; output to start partly in Q2 and fully in H2 FY27.
Base-case growth target of high-teens percentage per annum over the next 3-5 years; no revenue number given.
Base-business capex for FY27 about INR20 crore including maintenance, with INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex.
MBJ closing targeted around end-August 2026 with funding largely secured; Sanofi closing long-stop date June 2027, needing approvals in over 50 countries.
Hybrid power Phase 1 expected to go live in September 2026, Phase 2 about two months later; management expects EBITDA margin improvement.
Management expects some synergy projects with MBJ within the first year.
capex_capacity: Fermentation capacity has been roughly doubled (additional 540 KL); some capacity is for R&D and cGMP pilot facilities. Management said utilisation is effectively 0 or 100 and all output must be commercialised.
API block output started only recently, with fermentation constraints having delayed it by about two years versus the November 2023 guidance of FY25.
Gross block incremental INR370 crore over three years, of which about INR200 crore is fermentation and API facilities (asset turn 1.4-1.5x).
Hybrid power project is in progress and expected to lower power costs.
demand_pricing: Management said FY26 was stable and that the company was sold out on capacity; one year saw a dip due to excessive rains and power fluctuations.
Rifampicin to Rifapentine market shift is slower than hoped; management said Rifa-S demand is unaffected because GTBL is ready with both APIs.
A dispute with Optimus Drugs, a major customer, has been resolved and business is restarting; management said other buyers were available and capacity was sold out during the suspension.
Management said the company aims to sell intermediates to other Indian and global API makers to reduce customer concentration.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there nearly a three-year gap in earnings calls, and why was the API block revenue delayed from FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was flat but sold out; capex was late by about a year. API could not start because intermediate capacity was fully contracted to long-term customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR3,000 crore acquisition make sense given interest costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sanofi deal is expected to close later, with long-stop June 2027, and that interest rates in the target geographies are much lower than 10%. It said the business is cash-flow positive from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure for the MBJ and Sanofi deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raise of up to INR1,000 crore is planned; the debt component is undecided and will depend on the optimal mix, with options kept open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the base business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex remains, and total base-business capex including maintenance is about INR20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path from Sanofi brands to manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: A 3-year transition services agreement will move marketing authorisations country by country, with manufacturing moved to CMOs; management hopes for faster transfer, with tech transfer complete in year 1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Themis Medicare merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an external strategy review led it to focus on a fermentation-based CDMO and avoid diluting focus with predominantly domestic businesses.

risks_watch: Funding and leverage: INR1,000 crore equity planned; debt amount undecided. Interest and dilution implications are open.
Integration and bandwidth risk from two acquisitions across different geographies, plus a promoter pledge that management said should fall significantly within 12-15 months.
Sanofi closing timing depends on approvals in more than 50 countries, with long-stop June 2027. MBJ closing around end-August 2026 still needs final approvals.
ADCs have no CDMO project yet; MBJ revenue by vertical is undisclosed.
Sanofi margin uplift depends on integrating GTBL's own API; management said margins would return to current levels after stabilisation.
Customer concentration and the Optimus Drugs dispute; the settlement terms were not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and strategic on the long-term CDMO vision, but evasive on specifics: MBJ and Sanofi revenue, debt quantum, Optimus dispute details and promoter pledge data were withheld or left vague. Management also sounded defensive about the three-year gap in calls and the earlier API delays.
key_quotes: from a fermentation perspective, it's 0 or 100. So basically, we will be running capacity at full scale.
We are simply bringing in the synergies in both the places, which can add value, whereby 1 plus 1 is equal to more -- significantly more than 2.
